title: Forms & validation
summary: Cover the registration form like a tester: one negative test (empty submit shows every error) and one positive test (valid data creates the account).
why: Validation rules are where manual testers find most bugs. Automating both the negative and the positive path stops regressions on either side.
objectives: Negative: submit empty → 'Full name is required', 'Enter a valid email address', 'Age must be between 18 and 120', 'You must accept the terms'
Positive: fill, selectOption, check radio + checkbox → success message
hints: Errors are plain text: page.getByText('Full name is required')
pitfalls: Testing only the happy path — a form that stops validating still passes.
Using fill() on a checkbox (use check()).
teachAlong: Cause: one negative + one positive test.
Effect: a form that stops validating is caught.
Gate: the app is re-run with validation switched off — your negative test must fail there.

requires.reason: Tick the radio/checkbox with .check() (not click or fill) so Playwright verifies the new state.

mutants.reason: the form accepts empty and invalid input
